_doc: The fish photo judgements (judging/FISH.md, the rubric): python3 tools/fish_judge.py writes them into fish-photos.json (e, jt, c).
photos: teaching id -> {photo id (fish-photos.json f): code}. A code is view (p profile, o oblique, h head-on, t tail, d from above), whole (1, 0 partial),
light (g good, d dim or dark, n night or flash on black), colour loss (0 none, 1 slight: other colours still visible, 2 strong, 3 monochrome: only blue or green),
clarity (s sharp, m soft, b blurred or murky), size (l large, m medium, s small), count (1 one fish, s several of one kind, m other kinds too, x subject unclear),

flags (j juvenile, c camouflage, a out of water), then the ease 1-5. The tool adds the phase flag p for the entries fish.json marks dimorph, and caps the ease (judging/FISH.md "Caps"; the phase flag caps nothing since 2026-11-04).

crops: photo id -> a proposed crop [left, top, right, bottom] as fractions of the photo (curation.json crop's format), when the fish is small in the frame or the margins distract. A proposal for the admin only: never applied by the app or a script.

add: teaching id -> photo objects (fish-photos.json's shape) the pass added for a circle-1 entry short of very easy photos (Pierre, 2026-11-04: at least 5 each): research-grade candidates of fish-cand.json (tools/fetch_fish.py, PR #463: CC0, CC BY or CC BY-NC, the Indo-West Pacific), looked at and judged like the others; only the very easy ones needed were added (to 6 where enough were found). The tool appends them once, by observation.
passes: who judged what, how, and when. A photo of fish-photos.json not listed here is not judged yet (no e: it starts at difficulty 0).

passes.how: first look: contact sheets of 12 (tools/fish_judge.py --sheets), each photo at 300 x 225 px from the iNaturalist medium size (500 px), the observer's species name as a hint; second look (rubric 2: colour loss in place of a cast, crops): sheets of 20 at 240 x 180 px with a 5 x 5 grid for the crop fractions, a machine estimate of the warm colours left shown as a hint and corrected by eye (they agreed exactly on 58% of the photos, within one level on 98%)

passes.scope: rubric 3 (the phase flag no longer caps the ease); 214 candidates of fish-cand.json for the 11 circle-1 entries under 5 very easy photos, 37 added
passes.how: sheets of 12 at 300 x 225 px with a 5 x 5 grid, from the iNaturalist medium size

passes.scope: rubric 4: the 18 juvenile photos of Spadefish and Sweetlips (fish.json juv "distinct") looked at again and their ease judged on the other criteria only

rubric 5: the juvenile classes (tools/fish_source.json juv); the photos of the show-early genera and of Boxfish looked at again (17): 3 juveniles re-judged without the juvenile cap, one Pomacanthus imperator photo tagged juvenile
circles 2 and 3 and the winks, the 20 entries out of circle 1 (475 photos): every photo judged on rubric 5; 48 crops proposed
passes.how: sheets of 12 at 300 x 225 px with a 5 x 5 grid (tools/fish_judge.py --sheets --todo), from the iNaturalist medium size; then the small fish (size s, or medium and alone) again at 400 x 300 px with a 10 x 10 grid for the crops

passes.scope: the photo list rebuilt with Pierre's own observations taking no priority (tools/fish_photos.py, Pierre 2026-11-06): 327 new photos; 172 took the judgement of the same iNaturalist photo as a judged candidate (suggest.json fish: its code, the reference point taken back), 155 judged on rubric 5; then, for the 4 circle-1 entries left under 5 very easy photos (Damselfish, Moorish Idol, Groupers, Goatfish), very easy candidates Pierre has in play (curation.json fish add, one per observation, the easiest and most reference-like first, whoever took them) added to 6 (add)
passes.how: sheets of 12 at 300 x 225 px with a 5 x 5 grid, from the iNaturalist medium size (tools/fish_judge.py --sheets --todo, the tiles regrouped 12 to a sheet)

passes.scope: every compatible photo of Pierre's own in the pool (Pierre, Q148), the other observers' 24 per entry no longer sharing room with his: 250 new photos; 174 took the judgement of the same iNaturalist photo as a judged candidate (suggest.json fish), 76 judged on rubric 5
passes.how: sheets of 12 at 300 x 225 px, from the iNaturalist medium size

passes.scope: the units' reference photos (tools/fish_refs.py: what iNaturalist shows to represent each game species, circle-1 genus and family, its cover and taxon-page photos, and FishBase's photos, passing the game photo rules) of the four starter entries (Damselfish, Butterflyfish, Angelfish, Surgeonfish & Unicornfish): 308 photos judged on rubric 5, on what they show: every reference photo of these entries; only those judged at the reference level play (tools/fish_judge.py ref_level); the other entries' reference photos wait for the next pass
passes.how: sheets of 12 at 300 x 225 px with a 5 x 5 grid, from the iNaturalist medium size (tools/fish_judge.py --sheets --refs --todo)

passes.scope: the units' reference photos, batch 1: for the 23 other circle-1 entries, every species' iNaturalist cover and FishBase main picture that passes the game photo rules (tools/fish_refs.json from cover, or rep fishbase): 129 photos judged on rubric 5, on what they show; only those judged at the reference level play
passes.how: sheets of 12 at 300 x 225 px with a 5 x 5 grid, from the iNaturalist medium size and FishBase's file (tools/fish_judge.py --sheets --refs --todo, the small entries' tiles regrouped 12 to a sheet)

passes.scope: the units' reference photos, batch 2: every remaining reference photo of Moorish Idol, Pufferfish, Lionfish, Boxfish and Triggerfish (57 photos) judged on rubric 5; only those judged at the reference level play
passes.how: sheets of 12 at 300 x 225 px with a 5 x 5 grid (tools/fish_judge.py --sheets --refs --todo)

passes.scope: the units' reference photos, batch 3: every remaining reference photo of Groupers, Snapper, Goatfish, Sweetlips, Anthias and Bream (141 photos) judged on rubric 5; only those judged at the reference level play
passes.how: sheets of 12 at 300 x 225 px with a 5 x 5 grid (tools/fish_judge.py --sheets --refs --todo)
